place.source_title: Hartford City Public Library, 314 North High Street

brief: Carnegie library of 1904 in Neo-Classical style: one storey over a raised basement, buff brick with stone trim, a recessed entrance between paired Ionic columns under a pediment with a fanlight, reached by a wide flight of steps; a squat chimney and hipped roof behind a parapet. Record: 3 Commons photos plus 9 HABS measured drawing sheets.

facade.notes: the Hartford City IN Carnegie library (1904): one storey over a raised basement in buff brick with stone quoins, a recessed entry between paired Ionic columns under a lunette, a later rear addition and an access ramp; a lawn with flower beds

why.note: Carnegie grants (1883-1919) built most small-town libraries: one storey over a raised basement, a central entrance, the town paying the site and upkeep
a civic building is a raised, symmetric block set apart by steps, lawn and a portico: the public building as a temple
